sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate differs from the previously known C. fairchildi in that the latter has a narrower head, smaller eyes and shorter, narrower wings; it differs from C. nigriceps in that the latter has a wider head and shorter, narrower wings. The alate of this species has a yellowish brown head, a pale yellow pronotum with brown spots, oval ocelli touching the eyes, and 13-segmented antennae with segment 3 longer than or nearly equal to segment 2.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head yellowish brown; pronotum pale yellow with brown spots; antennae pale yellow; legs pale yellow; abdominal sternites light yellow. Head and pronotum with a few scattered erect setae. Eyes small, shape as figured; ocelli oval, touching the eyes; antennae 13-segmented, segment 3 longer than or nearly equal to segment 2, segment 4 shorter than segment 3. Pronotum equal to or slightly narrower than the head, anterior margin shallowly concave, sides rounded, posterior margin very slightly incurved at the middle, posterolateral margins rounded or straight. Media of the hindwing arising from the radial sector beyond the wing scale, about 0.68—0.90 mm from the suture. Measurements (mm, Trinidad morphotype series / series from Trinidad, St. Vincent, St. Lucia and elsewhere): head length to the apex of the labrum 1.11—1.20 / 1.09—1.20; head length to the lateral base of the mandible 0.90—0.92 / 0.86—0.90; head width 0.96—0.98 / 0.94—0.98; eye diameter 0.32 / 0.32—0.36; distance from the eye to the lower margin of the head 0.14—0.16 / 0.13—0.16; ocellus length 0.07—0.09 / 0.07—0.11; pronotum midlength 0.51—0.53 / 0.49—0.53; maximum pronotum length 0.60—0.64 / 0.56—0.60; pronotum width 0.83—0.88 / 0.79—0.86; hind tibia length 0.83 / 0.75—0.79; forewing length from the suture 6.29—6.50 / 5.58—6.08; forewing width 1.78—1.80 / 1.61—1.76.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Silvestri 1901 described this species from the soldier only; its alate had not been described before. The alate is described here for the first time (morphotype series collected in Maracas Valley, Trinidad). Synonymy: Calotermes temnocephalus Silvestri 1901, 1903 (soldier, nymph); Calotermes (?Procryptotermes) temnocephalus Holmgren 1911; Kalotermes (Glyptotermes) temnocephalus Emerson 1925; Calcaritermes temnocephalus Snyder 1949, 1959.
